public_rationale: Marcus said AI-made-up citations in legal filings were 'a routine occurrence', not an anomaly. He pointed to cases from May 2025. Business Insider, using Charlotin's database, reported that judges flagged at least 23 cases of AI hallucinations in court records between May 1 and May 27, 2025. That is nearly one a day. Lawyers or other legal professionals were at fault in at least 13 of them. The database had 73 such rulings in the first five months of 2025, against 37 in all of 2024. A dated example: on May 6, 2025, a court sanctioned two law firms, including K&L Gates, over a brief with fake authorities. Many separate findings across courts in a single month fit the plain meaning of 'routine' and contradict the 'anomaly' view. In October 2025, Charlotin said there were about two such cases a week before spring 2025 and two or three a day by October.
limitations: 'Routine' has no stated threshold; I read it as many separate incidents per month.
The May 2025 count is reported by Business Insider from Charlotin's data, not counted directly by me.
Some of the May cases involved self-represented litigants, not lawyers.
The counts show how often courts caught the problem, not what share of all filings had it.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: in spring 2025, courts were finding AI-made-up citations in legal filings again and again, across many unrelated cases and courts. They were not a rare, one-off anomaly.
He named no period. The context ('just this month') points to May 2025, the month of the post. I use May 2025 as the target period.
He named no number. I treat 'routine' as met if public records show many separate court findings within that month, on the order of several per week, across different courts and filers.
The claim is about whether such incidents happen often. It is not a claim about what share of all filings contain them.
criteria.support_condition: Dated court records or compilations show many independent court findings of AI-hallucinated citations in May 2025 (for example, dozens in the month, across different courts and filers, including lawyers).
criteria.contradiction_condition: Records show only isolated or very rare court findings of AI-fabricated citations in May 2025 (for example, a handful at most), consistent with an anomaly rather than a regular pattern.
